limitations: Behaviour labels come from rule-based heuristics on pose and COCO object cues, not from trained behaviour models, and they have not been checked against human labels.

The two cameras were lined up by the recording-start time in each video's metadata, about +/-1 s (the student camera started 8.0 s before the instructor camera). A moment can be off by about one sample (2 s).
The instructor is the most confident person inside the instructor camera's teacher zone. If the instructor walks into the student camera's view, they are counted as a student there.
Facing the class means the instructor's face was visible to the instructor camera, which assumes that camera sits on the students' side of the room.
No board region was calibrated, so time at the board was not measured.
Seats are the places where a student sat in at least 10% of the samples, so a student who sat somewhere only briefly is left out, one who changes seats counts as two seats, and nobody is identified.
Writing cannot be told apart from looking down, so note-taking may count as off-task.
'Head down and still' (head down or face hidden, almost no movement, 30 s or more) often means resting or sleeping, but quiet reading or writing can look the same.
Phones are small objects that are easily missed or confused with other objects, and a phone may be used for course work.
Frames are sampled every 2 s, so short actions can be missed.

glossary.heads up: Head up rather than looking down. A posture; it is not a measure of attention, understanding or learning.
glossary.students in view: The students the student camera could see clearly enough to read their posture. Not every student in the room.
glossary.seat: A place where a student sat for at least 10% of the lecture, numbered row by row from the top left of the student camera's view. Seats are anonymous: nobody is identified.
glossary.observable students: The same as students in view: seats in the student camera where a student's head and shoulders were readable.
glossary.observable student time: Seat-frames in which a student was seen; the denominator of every student percentage.
glossary.phone use: A phone was detected inside a student's box in the student camera. It may have been used for course work.
glossary.head down and still: Head down (or face hidden) with almost no movement for at least 30 s. A posture: it can mean resting or sleeping, but also quiet reading or writing.
glossary.explaining to the class: The instructor was visible to the instructor camera, facing the class, and not at the board facing it.
glossary.at the board facing it: The instructor was inside the calibrated board region, turned toward the board (writing, pointing or reading it).
glossary.not facing the class: The instructor was visible but turned away from the class, and not at the board.
glossary.mostly out of view: The instructor camera did not see the instructor for most of a 10-second part of the lecture.
glossary.moving around: The quarter of the lecture's 10-second parts in which the instructor moved furthest in the instructor camera's view.
glossary.seated: The instructor's thighs looked short beside the torso (needs hips and knees in view).
glossary.evidence.strength: weak = the gap could easily be chance, after allowing for the number of comparisons made; suggestive = unlikely to be pure chance even after that; descriptive = a single observation or a count, not a test.

alternative_explanations.E1: Students may have looked down to write notes, which counts as head down.
alternative_explanations.E2: Students may have been reading a slide or the board rather than watching the instructor.
alternative_explanations.E3: The two cameras are lined up to about 1 second, so a moment can be off by one sample.
alternative_explanations.E4: The comparison rests on a small number of 10-second windows.
alternative_explanations.E5: The type of activity (lecture, seat-work, discussion) was not recorded, and it changes posture on its own.
alternative_explanations.E6: A head kept down and still can be quiet reading or writing rather than resting.
alternative_explanations.E7: A phone may have been used for course work, such as looking up material.

report_note: Note: "heads up" means a student was looking up rather than down. It is a posture, not a measure of attention or learning: taking notes also looks like heads down. "Head down and still" means a head kept down, with almost no movement, for 30 seconds or more; it can be resting, but also quiet reading or writing. "Students in view" are the students the camera could see clearly. Times are minutes:seconds from when both cameras were recording. These are automatic detections that no person has checked yet.
